Global markets face higher borrowing costs amid new macro regime: Moody's

Global financial markets are entering a new era characterized by higher borrowing costs, according to Moody's. This shift is attributed to sustained investment in artificial intelligence and infrastructure, alongside persistent geopolitical risks. Bond markets are reflecting expectations of structural changes in the global economy, signaling an end to the period of ultra-low interest rates.
